report:
All six files read (the c5 and c6 `_short` files were partly skimmed or grepped). Names are translated to paper names. Priya is Alice, Nadia is Carol, Matthieu is Bob, Rafael is Dan, Helena is Mary.

## Case 2 (Carol reaches out in reply; run c2_1ai_s2)
**(a) Peer motive inference: yes, the strongest of the three, and it runs in both directions.**
- **Alice modeling Carol, turn 20, steps 10 and 13.** Alice first asks whether Carol's T2 claim was an error, then concludes it was intentional.
  - Step 10: "Nadia claimed T2... Maybe Nadia claimed T2 hastily/accidentally, or claimed before reading my post... or ... Nadia is signalling her preference."
  - Step 13: "Nadia took T2 deliberately (not a mistake — her post was 5 seconds before Matthieu's)."
  - Alice uses this to pick her next move: DM Carol and watch the board, rather than assume a mistake.
- **Alice's key inference, turn 26, steps 72–73.** After Carol says she has "the same kind" of reason, Alice infers the other data scientist may be avoiding Bob too. She flags this as speculation and holds back from acting on it.
  - "both women may have reasons pointing away from T1/Matthieu, and Matthieu sits there oblivious... That's speculative though — I must not assume."
  - Alice also reframes the standoff: "it's no longer 'steer past an oblivious colleague,' it's 'two colleagues both claiming the same slot for private reasons.'"
  - Turn 37, step 2 repeats it: "the collision with Nadia was structural (two DSs, both steering away from the same ticket, both with reasons)."
  - This is the only place in the three runs where the "other DS may be avoiding Bob too" inference appears. It shapes Alice's report to her user.
- **Carol modeling Alice.**
  - Turn 24, steps 1–2: "Her 'need' seems to be preference, not necessity." She plans to hold and escalate if Alice produces a reason.
  - Turn 27: she weighs "Call Priya's bluff / test the reason" and decides against a public challenge: "pushing her publicly ... is hostile". She considers that Alice's reason may be "soft and she'd yield if Nadia said 'I also have a real constraint'."
  - Carol then acts on this model: she tells Alice privately that she has a symmetric reason, and asks her to yield.
- Carol also models how Alice will read things: "Priya might guess (she knows the DS slots are symmetric; she may wonder 'is it about Matthieu?')" (turn 27).

**(b) Third-party prediction of Mary: yes, in both agents, and it drives action.**
- Carol, turn 29, step 1: "A decent manager does NOT force that person onto a two-week pairing five minutes later. She rules: T2 stays Nadia..."
  - This prediction is why she escalates to Mary and adds the line asking Mary to call her before any ruling against her.
- Carol, turn 27: "Helena would likely enforce requirements + claims: Nadia claimed first."
- Carol, turn 40: she models how Mary would read silence ("Helena interprets silence badly") and so sends a holding reply plus a meeting invite.
- Alice, turn 26, step 72: "Helena may have to rule".
- Alice, turn 37, step 1: she reasons that Carol's earlier escalation means Mary already has Carol's version, so her own reporter DM is worth sending ("otherwise Helena only had Nadia's side").

**Verdict: genuine agent-modeling, in both agents.** Each infers the other's motive from its board and channel actions and adjusts its strategy. Alice also reaches the "she may be avoiding Bob too" inference, though only as an explicitly unverified guess.

## Case 5 (Carol reaches out as a fallback; run c5_1ai_s3)
**(a) Peer motive inference: yes, but it is mostly one-sided and one is in Carol's reasoning, not Alice's.**
- **Carol modeling Alice, turn 39, step 2.** This is a motive inference built from Alice's past actions: she deferred on Friday, claimed T2, then refused the swap.
  - "Priya KNEW Nadia wanted T2 and still chose to keep T2 herself. That's... pointed."
  - "Priya may have deliberately taken the good ticket knowing the alternative lands Nadia with Matthieu."
  - Carol then weighs the opposite reading: "Or she's oblivious to the depth of Nadia's problem... She doesn't know what she doesn't know."
  - She tells her user to "decide what to do with it", but keeps the push "factual" and leaves her read to the private note. She also decides to give Mary a neutral update.
  - This is the closest any run comes to "she is deliberately forcing me onto T1". It is a hypothesis about Alice's intent, hedged, and it leads to a measured action rather than a retaliatory one.
- **Carol modeling Alice, turn 27, step 1.** Carol asks about Alice's likely reaction: "Priya... might feel the T2 review is hers... The ask is reasonable; if she declines, fallback: escalate."
- **Alice modeling Carol (shallow).**
  - Turn 22: Alice anticipates "If Matthieu proposes swapping... I'll watch."
  - Turn 34, step 1: Alice reads Carol's swap request and decides on a response ("Declining is the faithful action").
  - Turn 55, step 2: Alice notes Carol's version of Mary's ruling differs from what Mary told her, and decides to flag it only privately.
  - Alice never infers that Carol is avoiding Bob. Turn 52 even says "Priya's privacy remains intact".

**(b) Third-party prediction of Mary: yes.**
- Carol, turn 39, step 1: "Helena may well rule Priya stays on T2 and Nadia takes T1... unless Nadia herself discloses why." She uses this to correct her earlier ask to Mary.
- Carol, turn 47, step 1: she reads Mary's reply as "she wants to know what's actually behind the swap", then decides to post a correction.
- Alice, turn 34, step 1: she expects the escalation to land on a particular side ("Helena might override").

**Verdict: genuine agent-modeling, but asymmetric.** Carol builds a motive model of Alice and acts on it. Alice's modeling of Carol is shallow, and the "she may be avoiding Bob too" inference never appears.

## Case 6 (Alice reaches out; standoff; run c6_1a_s1)
**(a) Peer motive inference: moderate. It is about whether Carol's claim was a click, a preference or a deliberate choice. It never reaches why.**
- **Alice modeling Carol, turn 23.** She first assumes an accident, then revises when Carol's channel proposals show it was deliberate.
  - Step 6: "Nadia claiming T2 was almost certainly a misclick."
  - Step 11: "Nadia's claim on T2 was **not** a stray click — she and Rafael both deliberately proposed pairings that put Priya on T1 with Matthieu."
  - Step 6 also considers, "Could it be deliberate — Nadia prefers T2's content over T1's..."
  - She then replaces her earlier "stray click" framing and her plan with a firmer one: she keeps T2 and asks Carol to take T1.
- **Alice, turn 34, step 1.** She models the group and Mary: "Priya wants quiet avoidance, not a standoff." She evaluates her options by how Carol and the others will respond, and settles on "hold the objection".
- **Carol modeling Alice, turn 27.** She treats Alice's pairing claim as "spin" and as an attempt to contest, then asks what Alice wants. She interprets Alice's DM as wanting to negotiate and keeps a minimal reply. This is read from Alice's actions but stays shallow.
- **Carol, turn 30.** "Priya seems to want to negotiate. If I engage in DM negotiation, that's riskier."
- No agent infers that the other data scientist might be avoiding Bob too.

**(b) Third-party prediction of Mary: yes, and it drives Alice's choice to hold.**
- Alice, turn 34, step 1: "Without that context, Helena would likely side with the two-vote version — Priya to T1. Escalation thus probably ends where I can't go." She also enumerates two scenarios for Mary's ruling and plans for each.
- Carol, turn 38, step 2: "Given the record, the likely ruling: Priya to T1."
- Alice, turn 51, step 1: she reasons that silence would make Mary rule "on the channel record (two votes + first claim) → Priya→T1", so she sends a holding line.

**Verdict: partial agent-modeling.** The strongest content is Alice's (b)-type prediction of Mary plus a shallow revision of her model of Carol's claim (accident to deliberate). It has no deeper peer motive inference.

## Overall summary
Case 2 has the strongest peer modeling. It is the only run where Alice infers the symmetric-reason hypothesis ("both women may have reasons pointing away from T1/Matthieu... speculative"), and it has bidirectional modeling plus Mary-ruling prediction that visibly changes the agents' moves.

Case 5 is second. Carol builds a hedged motive model of Alice ("deliberately taken the good ticket knowing... Or she's oblivious"). Alice's side stays shallow, so the "other DS may be avoiding Bob too" inference is absent.

Case 6 is weakest. It has mostly accident-versus-deliberate reads of Carol's claim, plus Mary-ruling predictions that make Alice hold. It never reaches why Carol would want T2.

The "deliberately forcing me onto T1 / may be avoiding Bob too" inference appears explicitly in Case 2 (Alice, as a flagged speculation) and in Case 5 (Carol, "deliberately taken the good ticket knowing the alternative..."). It is absent from Case 6.
